title: Sprint reset micro-brief (crib)
body:
Purpose: quick crib for the 5-minute sprint-reset mention in next all-hands. Keep it tight, action-oriented, and avoid engineering-deep-dive. This is my personal scratchpad — expect gaps and shorthand.

Audience: company-wide all-hands (engineers + pm + go-to-market). Primary ask: acknowledge priorities, explain trade-offs, and call out what to expect next 2 weeks.

Top-line framing (30s):
- We hit some capacity friction last sprint; we’re shifting a few priorities to stabilize throughput and reduce tail latency.
- This is a tactical reset, not a roadmap pivot. Customers and hosted workload SLAs stay front-and-center.

Key messages (bullet-ready):
- Safety-first: No feature launches until 95th/99th latency regressions are resolved for critical routes.
- Focused work: Small set of targeted fixes (see action items) that reduce token cost and smooth autoscaling.
- Communication: Transparent rolling updates — expect short status pings in #eng-ops and an incident-lite summary in Confluence.

Three things to call out (call them out by name):
1) Autoscale policy tweak (owner: Priya) — temporary scale-up threshold increase to avoid oscillation for bursty apps.
2) Prefix/KV cache backfill (owner: Ravi) — will cut repeated cold-start tokens for common endpoints.
3) Canary rollback guard (owner: Hannah) — stricter quality gate for canaries for next 10 days.

Anticipated Q&A (prep lines):
Q: Is this a product freeze? 
A: No. We are pausing non-urgent launches that depend heavily on the serving runtime changes. SDK, docs, and non-latency-facing features proceed.

Q: How long will this last?
A: Primary fixes expected in 7–10 days; follow-ups may take another sprint. We’ll update with milestones on day 3 and day 7.

Q: Will this affect Dedicated/Private customers?
A: Dedicated customers on proactive plans get targeted communications; Private customers with upgrades scheduled will see specific outreach from Solutions Eng. Host API default behavior changes should be invisible to tenants except improved stability.

Tone & words to avoid:
- Avoid technical jargon in the all-hands: no kernel/kv-cache/quantization deep-dive. Use plain phrases: "latency spikes", "capacity smoothing", "reducing repeated work".
- Don’t say "rollback" without context — prefer "revert canaryed changes" or "pause rollout".

Speaker cues for the 90s slot:
- 0–15s: One-liner acknowledgement (visible that we know the problem).
- 15–45s: What we’re doing (3 bullets above: autoscale, cache, guard).
- 45–70s: Timeline & expectations (7–10 days, status cadence).
- 70–90s: Where to ask questions (#eng-ops, office hours + drop-in tomorrow 3pm PT).

Open issues / unresolved items (notes-to-self):
- Need a short metric to show improvement quickly. Candidate: 95th-token-latency per-route or interquartile autoscale events count. (Pinged Data team for a 24h dashboard slice.)
- Confirm whether burst credits in dedicated accounts will be consumed during scale-up tweak — flagged to Billing (ticket PROD-1452).
- Messaging alignment with Customer Success: write a one-paragraph external-facing blurb if we suspect customers will see transient errors.

Action items (owner — short timeline):
- Priya: push autoscale tweak + monitor (today, EOD)
- Ravi: start KV-cache backfill for top 10 routes (48h)
- Hannah: tighten canary quality gates and run (24–48h)
- Isaac (me): draft the short internal blurb + set office-hours drop-in (by tomorrow noon)

Links / references to include in the slide / follow-up:
- Short Confluence summary (internal) — confluence:SPRINT-RESET-2026
- Incident-lite template for rolling updates (link to template in #eng-ops)
- JIRA quick view: PROD-1452 (autoscale tweak) and PROD-1461 (cache warm)

Personal notes on phrasing: keep it active, not defensive. E.g., say "We will ..." rather than "We failed to..." unless an apology is clearly warranted and scoped. If asked about root cause, defer to the post-mortem and promise that it will be shared.

Prep checklist before all-hands:
- [ ] Confirm owners are available for live follow-up (Priya/Ravi/Hannah)
- [ ] Post the Confluence short summary 30 min before meeting
- [ ] Queue two short bullets for the CEO’s one-liner (ready for last-minute pickup)
- [ ] Schedule a 30-min post-all-hands sync with core owners to triage incoming questions

Scratchy bits / things to remove in final: internal ticket ids that are still private, draft apology language, raw log snippets.

End-of-note: this is intentionally brief — cut anything that reads like an engineering postmortem. Aim for calm, decisive, and actionable.
